Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara, added the fifth vow (Brahmacharya) to the existing code.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Confusing the Chaturyama (Parshvanatha) with the Pancha Mahavrata (Mahavira). Parshvanatha gave only four.
Assuming these vows apply equally to laypeople and monks. Laypeople follow Anuvratas (smaller vows), not the full Mahavratas.
Thinking Jainism invented these; the first four were pre-existing ascetic norms adapted by the Tirthankaras.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Context

  • Mahavira codified the five.
  • Rooted in Shramana tradition.

Personalities

  • Parshvanatha (4 vows)
  • Mahavira (added 1)

Core Doctrines Mindmap

  • 1. Ahimsa (Non-violence): Paramount principle; includes thoughts and speech.
  • 2. Satya (Truth): Speaking truth without causing injury.
  • 3. Asteya (Non-stealing): Avoiding taking anything not given.
  • 4. Aparigraha (Non-attachment): Detachment from worldly material possessions.
  • 5. Brahmacharya (Chastity): Added by Mahavira; sexual restraint.
VowMeaning
AhinsaNon-Injury
SatyaTruthfulness
AsteyaNon-Stealing
AparigrahaNon-Possession
BrahmacharyaCelibacy
